name: Non-Ossifying Fibroma
definition: Common benign fibrous metaphyseal bone lesion in children and adolescents that usually resolves with skeletal maturation.

investigations.principle: Radiographs are usually diagnostic; advanced imaging is rarely needed for classic lesions.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, infection, tumor or occult-injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

green: Activity advice if large/high fracture risk
amber: Large symptomatic lesions or pathological fracture may require curettage/fixation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Asthi lesion phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Common benign fibrous metaphyseal bone lesion in children and adolescents that usually resolves with skeletal maturation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, major trauma, suspected infection, pathological fracture, neurovascular compromise or other listed red flags.
